key_insight: CARE lets LLMs improve experiment selection indirectly by auditing evidence before they can override a reliable non-LLM incumbent policy.
engineering_relevance: This design is relevant for high-stakes scientific automation because it preserves optimization gains while reducing unsafe or irreversible experiment choices.
method: Keep a non-LLM incumbent optimizer as the default action path
Use an LLM to revise challenger ranking policies instead of directly selecting experiments
Apply a public-evidence intervention gate and record each decision in an audit log
evidence_signal: The abstract reports stronger final-best results than the public incumbent on both benchmarks, improving from 80.0 to 88.5 on Minerva/Olympus and from 83.9 to 92.1 on ChemLex.
watch_item: The approach depends on the quality and sufficiency of pre-outcome public evidence, so weak evidence may limit when the LLM is allowed to intervene.
paper_title: CARE: Controlling LLM-Generated Policies through Auditable Review of Evidence in Scientific Experimentation
